<!-- Generated by TestCLIReferenceDrift (cmd/kudurru) from the command tree; do not edit. Run `make docs-gen`. -->

One binary is the server, the supervisors and the client. The client verbs
talk to the REST API of a server chosen by `--server` or a context saved by
`kudurru login`; `kudurru admin` talks to the local admin socket instead. The
same text is available offline as `kudurru <command> --help`.

## Global flags

Every command accepts these flags.

```text
      --ca-file string             PEM bundle to trust for the API server
      --cli-config string          CLI contexts file (default $KUDURRU_CLI_CONFIG or
                                   ~/.config/kudurru/config.yaml)
      --config string              path to the server's kudurru.yaml (default
                                   "/etc/kudurru/kudurru.yaml")
      --context string             CLI context to use (default: the current context, or
                                   $KUDURRU_CONTEXT)
      --insecure-skip-tls-verify   do not verify the server's TLS certificate (lab use only)
  -n, --namespace string           namespace for namespaced kinds (default: the context's,
                                   else "default")
  -o, --output string              output format: table, wide, json, yaml or name
      --request-timeout duration   timeout of each API request (default 30s)
      --server string              API server URL, e.g. https://dns.example (overrides the
                                   context; env KUDURRU_SERVER)
      --token string               API token kdr_… (overrides the context; env KUDURRU_TOKEN)
```

## kudurru admin

Break-glass operations over the server's unix socket (default /run/kudurru/kudurru.sock). They do not use the API or a token: the server admits root, its own user (65532 in the distroless image, which is what docker exec and kubectl exec get), or a configured group.

```text
docker exec kudurru kudurru admin reset-password admin
kubectl exec -n dns deploy/kudurru -- kudurru admin create-token --expires-in 1h
```

Flags:

```text
      --protocol string   socket protocol: auto, http or ndjson (default "auto")
      --socket string     admin socket path (default $KUDURRU_ADMIN_SOCKET or
                          /run/kudurru/kudurru.sock)
```

### kudurru admin create-token

Mint an API token and print it once on stdout. Without --user the token belongs to the built-in break-glass service account and expires after 24h unless --expires-in says otherwise; with --user it is a personal token of that local user.

```text
kudurru admin create-token [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --description string   what the token is for
      --expires-in string    lifetime, e.g. 1h (default 24h for break-glass tokens)
      --user string          local user owning the token (default: the break-glass service account)
```

### kudurru admin list-users

List local users.

```text
kudurru admin list-users
```

### kudurru admin reset-password

Set a local user's password and require a change at the next login. Without --password the server generates one and prints it once. The username defaults to the built-in admin; --create makes that account when it does not exist.

```text
kudurru admin reset-password [username] [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --create            create the user (as the built-in admin) when it does not exist
      --password string   new password (default: generated by the server)
      --password-stdin    read the new password from stdin
      --revoke-tokens     also revoke every API token of the user (a reset alone revokes
                          sessions, not tokens)
```

## kudurru api

Send a raw request to the API (path relative to /api/v1).

```text
kudurru api <method> <path> | api <path> [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru api /version
kudurru api POST /cache/flush
kudurru api PATCH /settings --data '{"cache":{"maxEntries":200000}}'
kudurru api POST /apply --data @zones.json
```

Flags:

```text
      --content-type string   Content-Type of the body (default application/json)
  -d, --data string           request body: inline text, @file, or @- for stdin
  -H, --header stringArray    extra header Name: value (repeatable)
```

## kudurru apply

Create or update objects from manifests. Documents may be multi-document YAML, JSON objects, JSON arrays or a List. Every document is a whole object applied with manager "api" (POST /api/v1/apply); objects owned by a file or an integration are refused with "managed\_by" and the owner.

```text
kudurru apply -f file|dir|- [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru apply -f zones.yaml
kudurru apply -f objects.d/ -R
cat lists.yaml | kudurru apply -f -
```

Flags:

```text
  -f, --filename stringArray   file, directory or - for stdin (repeatable)
  -R, --recursive              descend into subdirectories of -f directories
```

## kudurru audit

Show the audit log of API writes.

```text
kudurru audit [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --actor string   principal name
      --kind string    object kind
      --limit int      maximum entries (default 100)
      --name string    object name
      --since string   RFC 3339 time or a duration back from now (24h)
```

### kudurru audit keys

Manage an operator-protected 0600 ring file. Publish it separately as the ring.json entry of audit.keySecret in the release namespace. These commands never contact a server or print private material. Back up the ring and AuditLog history separately; ordinary configuration backups contain neither.

Before upgrading existing AuditLog storage, explicitly import each retained legacy master-key file and set a past --legacy-before cutoff. Missing old keys cannot be recovered. Rotation preserves public keys; revocation withdraws trust in affected history. Keep the containing directory private and do not remove the persistent .lock file while commands may run.

#### kudurru audit keys init

Initialize an explicitly cluster-bound ring.

```text
kudurru audit keys init [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --cluster-id string            Original kube-system namespace UID (required)
      --file string                  Private ring file (required; 0600)
      --legacy-before string         Past whole-second RFC3339 cutoff; legacy objects must
                                     predate it
      --legacy-master-file strings   Explicit protected legacy master-key files (maximum 16)
      --namespace string             AuditLog release namespace (required)
```

#### kudurru audit keys revoke

Withdraw trust in a retained signer.

```text
kudurru audit keys revoke [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --file string     Private ring file (required; 0600)
      --key-id string   Retained public-key fingerprint to revoke
      --legacy          Withdraw trust in all imported legacy HMAC keys
```

#### kudurru audit keys rotate

Replace the signer and retain old public keys.

```text
kudurru audit keys rotate [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --file string   Private ring file (required; 0600)
```

### kudurru audit verify

Ask the server to verify the complete retained audit trail and available batch seals. Requires audit.read and an audit license. The server caches verification results for 30 seconds; checkedAt identifies the scan.

Use -o json for a structured result. Exits nonzero for an integrity failure, unavailable verification, or denied access.

```text
kudurru audit verify
```

## kudurru backup

Save every object (zones, record sets, lists, client groups, policies) as a multi-document YAML file. Status and server-set metadata are dropped so the file re-applies cleanly with `kudurru restore -f`. --safe redacts credentials embedded in URLs (user:password@ and token/key/secret query parameters) so the file can be shared; such a backup needs the secrets filled in before restore.

```text
kudurru backup --out file.yaml [--safe] [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --exclude-managed   skip objects owned by files or integrations
      --out string        file to write (- for stdout)
      --safe              redact credentials embedded in URLs
```

## kudurru blocking

Show or toggle blocking.

### kudurru blocking disable

Turn blocking off, indefinitely or for a duration (30s, 5m, 1h).

```text
kudurru blocking disable [duration] [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --until string   re-enable at this RFC 3339 time
```

### kudurru blocking enable

Turn blocking on.

```text
kudurru blocking enable
```

### kudurru blocking status

Show whether blocking is on.

```text
kudurru blocking status
```

## kudurru cache

Manage the response cache.

### kudurru cache flush

Flush the whole cache, or the entries of one name.

```text
kudurru cache flush [name]
```

## kudurru completion

Generate a shell completion script.

```text
bash:        source <(kudurru completion bash)
zsh:         kudurru completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_kudurru"
fish:        kudurru completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/kudurru.fish
powershell:  kudurru completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

```text
kudurru completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell
```

## kudurru delete

Delete objects by name or by manifest.

```text
kudurru delete (<kind> <name...> | -f file|dir|-) [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru delete zone lab-example-com
kudurru delete rrset web -n apps
kudurru delete -f zones.yaml
```

Flags:

```text
  -f, --filename stringArray   file, directory or - naming the objects to delete
      --ignore-not-found       treat a missing object as deleted
  -R, --recursive              descend into subdirectories of -f directories
```

## kudurru describe

Show an object's spec, status conditions and diagnoses.

```text
kudurru describe <kind> <name>
```

## kudurru doctor

Check the local configuration and environment, then the API server:

```text
config     the config file parses and validates
dataDir    exists, is a directory, is writable, is not world-writable
ports      every configured listener address can be bound (or is in use by
           a running kudurru)
api        the API server answers (the CLI context, --server, or the local
           listeners.api.address)
token      the CLI token is accepted (GET /auth/me)
diagnoses  configuration diagnoses reported by the server (GET /info/messages)
database   with database.dsn set: the central database answers, runs
           PostgreSQL 16 or newer and has a schema this binary can use;
           warns about sslmode=disable to another host
vrrp       warns when `kudurru vip run --legacy` renders keepalived without
           auth_hmac (unauthenticated VRRP adverts); silent on nodes
           without keepalived
```

Exits non-zero when a check fails.

```text
kudurru doctor [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --keepalived-config kudurru vip run   keepalived.conf rendered by kudurru vip run
                                            (default "/etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf")
      --skip-api                            do not contact the API server
      --skip-ports                          do not test whether listener ports can be bound
      --vip-run-dir kudurru vip run         run directory shared with kudurru vip run
                                            (legacy-mode marker) (default "/run/kudurru")
```

## kudurru edge

dnsdist supervisor: render the configuration or run dnsdist (PID 1 of the kudurru-dnsdist image).

### kudurru edge render

Print the dnsdist configuration the supervisor would run (credentials are random per call).

```text
kudurru edge render [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --acl strings                         client prefixes allowed to query (default: private
                                            and loopback ranges)
      --api string                          dnsdist webserver/API address (loopback only)
                                            (default "127.0.0.1:8083")
      --api-key-group string                group (name or gid) of the --api-key-out file,
                                            e.g. keepalived_script; default unchanged
      --api-key-out string                  write the per-start dnsdist API key here (0640),
                                            e.g. /run/kudurru/dnsdist-api.key
      --authoritative-cache                 cache the authoritative pool briefly and flush it
                                            on zone serial changes
      --authoritative-cache-ttl int         max TTL (s) of the authoritative cache (default 30)
      --authoritative-zones strings         zones routed to the authoritative pool, in
                                            addition to those polled from /internal/zones
      --backend-port int                    kudurru DNS port for entries without a port and
                                            EndpointSlices without the named port (default 5353)
      --backend-port-name string            EndpointSlice port name carrying DNS (default "dns")
      --backends string                     static backends: comma-separated
                                            [name=]host[:port] (port default --backend-port);
                                            EVERY edge lists ALL kudurru nodes
      --backends-from string                membership source: static (from --backends) or
                                            endpointslice:<namespace>/<service> (default "static")
      --cache-size int                      resolver pool packet cache entries (default 200000)
      --console string                      dnsdist console address (loopback only) (default
                                            "127.0.0.1:5199")
      --doh string                          enable the DoH frontend on host:port (the host
                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);
                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends
                                            are do53 plus those given
      --doh3 string                         enable the DoH3 frontend on host:port (the host
                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);
                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends
                                            are do53 plus those given
      --doq string                          enable the DoQ frontend on host:port (the host
                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);
                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends
                                            are do53 plus those given
      --dot string                          enable the DoT frontend on host:port (the host
                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);
                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends
                                            are do53 plus those given
      --dynblocks                           enable dnsdist dynamic blocking
      --dynblocks-nxdomain-rate int         per-client NXDOMAIN rate that triggers a dynamic
                                            block; 0 disables (default 20)
      --dynblocks-qps int                   per-client query rate (qps over 10 s) that
                                            triggers a dynamic block (default 50)
      --ebpf                                push dynamic-block drops into an eBPF socket
                                            filter (needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN)
      --internal-port int                   kudurru internal listener port (zone serial
                                            polling); 0 disables (default 8082)
      --listen strings                      addresses every frontend binds (default [0.0.0.0])
      --out string                          write the rendered files into this directory
                                            instead of stdout
      --pool-authoritative string           load-balancing policy of the authoritative pool
                                            (default "leastOutstanding")
      --pool-resolver string                load-balancing policy of the resolver pool
                                            (default "chashed")
      --protocols strings                   frontends (do53,dot,doh,doq,doh3); default do53
                                            plus all TLS ones when --tls-dir is set
      --proxy-protocol-secret-file string   PROXYv2 TLV 0xE0 shared secret (printable, >= 32
                                            bytes: openssl rand -hex 32); required unless
                                            every backend is loopback
      --renderer string                     configuration format: yaml (dnsdist.yml +
                                            functions-only dnsdist.lua) or lua (dnsdist.conf)
                                            (default "yaml")
      --server-id string                    dnsdist general.server_id; default the host name
      --threads int                         Do53 listener threads (default 2)
      --tls-dir string                      directory with tls.crt+tls.key (or
                                            fullchain.pem+privkey.pem): enables
                                            DoT/DoH/DoQ/DoH3, watched for rotation
      --transfer-sources strings            addresses/prefixes allowed to send
                                            AXFR/IXFR/NOTIFY/UPDATE through the edge
```

```text
                                            addition to those polled from /internal/zones

                                            EndpointSlices without the named port (default 5353)

      --backends string                     static backends: comma-separated
                                            [name=]host[:port] (port default --backend-port);
                                            EVERY edge lists ALL kudurru nodes

      --doh string                          enable the DoH frontend on host:port (the host
                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);
                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends
                                            are do53 plus those given

                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);
                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends
                                            are do53 plus those given
      --doq string                          enable the DoQ frontend on host:port (the host
                                            must be a --listen address; the chart's form);

                                            with any of --dot/--doh/--doq/--doh3 the frontends

      --dynblocks-qps int                   per-client query rate (qps over 10 s) that
                                            triggers a dynamic block (default 50)
      --ebpf                                push dynamic-block drops into an eBPF socket
                                            filter (needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN)
      --health-address string               supervisor listener: /healthz/ready,

                                            derived from KUDURRU_ENCRYPTION_KEY)

      --pool-authoritative string           load-balancing policy of the authoritative pool
                                            (default "leastOutstanding")
      --pool-resolver string                load-balancing policy of the resolver pool
                                            (default "chashed")
      --protocols strings                   frontends (do53,dot,doh,doq,doh3); default do53
                                            plus all TLS ones when --tls-dir is set
      --proxy-protocol-secret-file string   PROXYv2 TLV 0xE0 shared secret (printable, >= 32
                                            bytes: openssl rand -hex 32); required unless
                                            every backend is loopback
      --readiness-address string            alias of --health-address (the chart's form)
                                            (default ":8084")
      --renderer string                     configuration format: yaml (dnsdist.yml +

      --server-id string                    dnsdist general.server_id; default the host name
```

## kudurru export

Print objects as re-appliable YAML (all kinds by default).

```text
kudurru export [kind...] [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --exclude-managed   skip objects owned by files or integrations
      --safe              redact credentials embedded in URLs
```

## kudurru get

List or show objects. Kinds and their aliases:

```text
dnszones       zone, zones, dnszone        (cluster-scoped)
dnsrecordsets  rrset, rrsets, dnsrecordset
blocklists     list, lists, blocklist, bl
clientgroups   cg, clientgroup
policies       pol, policy
```

```text
kudurru get <kind> [name...] [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru get zones
kudurru get rrset -A -o wide
kudurru get blocklist ads -n default -o yaml
kudurru get pol -l team=platform
```

Flags:

```text
  -A, --all-namespaces    list across all namespaces
  -l, --selector string   label selector, e.g. app=web,tier!=db
```

## kudurru health

Probe a running instance (Docker HEALTHCHECK; --vrrp is the keepalived check).

```text
kudurru health [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --dns string                              VIP address:port to probe over udp and tcp
                                                (loopback is probed while this node does not
                                                hold the VIP)
      --dnsdist-api string                      local dnsdist API; empty skips the backend
                                                check (default "http://127.0.0.1:8083")
      --dnsdist-api-key-file kudurru edge run   dnsdist API key published by kudurru edge run
                                                (default "/run/kudurru/dnsdist-api.key")
      --ops-address string                      ops listener to probe (default "127.0.0.1:8081")
      --qname string                            name queried for TXT (default
                                                "health.kudurru.internal.")
      --ready                                   probe readiness instead of liveness
      --require-backends int                    minimum number of dnsdist backends up (default 1)
      --timeout duration                        request timeout (with --vrrp: the probe
                                                budget, 900ms unless set) (default 3s)
      --vrrp kudurru vip probe                  run the keepalived VRRP probe (see kudurru vip
                                                probe)
```

## kudurru iam

Manage identity configuration and upgrades.

### kudurru iam migrate

Inspect or perform the offline Kubernetes IAM upgrade. Stop every old and new kudurru process, IAM writer and previous migrator before begin or resume. Install the new CRDs and back up the release namespace first. The commands use Kubernetes credentials directly; they do not connect to the kudurru API.

Original Secrets and private migration archives remain rollback artifacts. Output contains only state, object identifiers and counts, never credentials. An uncertain Create requires explicit operator recovery; resume never adopts a public object merely because its annotations or contents match.

Flags:

```text
      --kube-context string        Kubernetes context (default current kubeconfig context)
      --kubeconfig string          Kubernetes client configuration (default standard
                                   kubeconfig or in-cluster identity)
      --release-namespace string   required: namespace containing the original private IAM Secrets
      --timeout duration           whole operation deadline (maximum 30m) (default 5m0s)
```

#### kudurru iam migrate begin

Capture, archive and migrate while all IAM processes are stopped.

```text
kudurru iam migrate begin [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --offline   acknowledge that all IAM readers/writers and previous migrators are stopped
```

#### kudurru iam migrate plan

Validate the complete migration without writing.

```text
kudurru iam migrate plan
```

#### kudurru iam migrate resume

Resume an interrupted migration at an exact journal version.

```text
kudurru iam migrate resume [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --offline                   acknowledge that all IAM readers/writers and previous
                                  migrators are stopped
      --resource-version string   exact journal resource version returned by status (never
                                  inferred)
```

#### kudurru iam migrate status

Read the admission state and journal resource version.

```text
kudurru iam migrate status
```

## kudurru import

Import data from other DNS servers.

### kudurru import adguard

Convert a single YAML file (at most 4 MiB) without reading referenced files or fetching network sources. Use --file - for stdin. The default prints a partial conversion and a bounded loss report without contacting kudurru. Review unsupported semantics before --apply, which starts the existing tracked migration with normal validation, ownership and license checks. --wait requires --apply and returns the final result; without it, success means only that the job was accepted. Select objects and settings explicitly to limit application. Destination-derived targets (--use-vips or --update-nameservers) explicitly opt into destination access. No source credentials or file paths enter the plan or migration journal.

```text
kudurru import adguard --file PATH [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --apply                        start a tracked background migration of the reviewed
                                     conversion
      --dry-run                      preview only (the default)
  -f, --file string                  source YAML file; - reads stdin (maximum 4 MiB)
      --local-zone strings           explicit local suffixes to make authoritative for exact
                                     IP/CNAME rewrites
      --nameserver strings           replace imported authority with these DNS names
      --nameserver-address strings   generate authority from these serving IPs or VIPs
      --select-object strings        import only these Kind/[namespace/]name objects (repeatable)
      --select-setting strings       import only these top-level settings sections (repeatable)
      --skip-settings                leave settings unchanged
      --update-nameservers           derive authority from the destination context hostname or IP
      --use-vips                     use discovered destination VIPs (explicit destination API
                                     access)
      --wait                         wait for final migration results (requires --apply)
```

### kudurru import bind

Import a BIND zone file into a zone's record sets.

```text
kudurru import bind <zone> -f file.zone [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
  -f, --filename string   zone file in BIND presentation format, or - for stdin
      --origin string     zone apex, to create the DNSZone when it does not exist yet
```

### kudurru import blocky

Convert a single YAML file (at most 4 MiB) without reading referenced files or fetching network sources. Use --file - for stdin. The default prints a partial conversion and a bounded loss report without contacting kudurru. Review unsupported semantics before --apply, which starts the existing tracked migration with normal validation, ownership and license checks. --wait requires --apply and returns the final result; without it, success means only that the job was accepted. Select objects and settings explicitly to limit application. Destination-derived targets (--use-vips or --update-nameservers) explicitly opt into destination access. No source credentials or file paths enter the plan or migration journal.

```text
kudurru import blocky --file PATH [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --apply                        start a tracked background migration of the reviewed
                                     conversion
      --dry-run                      preview only (the default)
  -f, --file string                  source YAML file; - reads stdin (maximum 4 MiB)
      --nameserver strings           replace imported authority with these DNS names
      --nameserver-address strings   generate authority from these serving IPs or VIPs
      --select-object strings        import only these Kind/[namespace/]name objects (repeatable)
      --select-setting strings       import only these top-level settings sections (repeatable)
      --skip-settings                leave settings unchanged
      --update-nameservers           derive authority from the destination context hostname or IP
      --use-vips                     use discovered destination VIPs (explicit destination API
                                     access)
      --wait                         wait for final migration results (requires --apply)
```

### kudurru import decommission

Replace apex NS and SOA primary names in zones tracked by this migration, creating A/AAAA records when serving IPs or VIPs are selected. Preview using the destination hostname or IP by default, explicit --nameserver or --nameserver-address values, or --use-vips. Save the JSON output, then apply that reviewed file with --apply --plan-file. The source server is not shut down; update parent delegations and glue separately.

```text
kudurru import decommission <run-id> [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --apply                        apply a saved and reviewed cutover preview
      --nameserver strings           kudurru authoritative DNS names (repeatable; first
                                     becomes SOA primary)
      --nameserver-address strings   kudurru serving IPs or VIPs; generate in-zone NS names
                                     and A/AAAA records (repeatable)
      --plan-file string             JSON preview to apply (produce with -o json)
      --use-vips                     use discovered kudurru VIPs for nameservers and address
                                     records
```

### kudurru import pihole

Connect to the source API using its v6 application password. By default, print a preview containing converted objects, settings and warnings without changing either server. Add --apply to start a tracked background import on the selected kudurru server using its normal validation, ownership and license checks. Without --wait, exit status 0 means the server accepted the job, not that every item imported successfully. Scripts that need the final success/failure exit status must use --apply --wait. Use import runs RUN\_ID to inspect the report later. All items are selected by default; --select-object and --select-setting select only the named items. Inspect every result: writes are not transactional. Source credentials are never stored by kudurru.

```text
kudurru import pihole --source-url URL [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru import pihole --source-url http://dns.local --source-key-file ./source-key
kudurru import pihole --source-url http://dns.local --source-key-file ./source-key --apply
```

Flags:

```text
      --apply                             start a tracked background import of the converted
                                          configuration
      --dry-run                           preview only (the default)
      --local-zone strings                local DNS suffixes to make authoritative (default:
                                          Pi-hole's local domain)
      --nameserver strings                kudurru authoritative DNS names; replace imported NS
                                          and SOA primary (repeatable; first is primary)
      --nameserver-address strings        kudurru serving IPs or VIPs; generate in-zone NS
                                          names and A/AAAA records (repeatable)
      --select-object strings             import only these Kind/[namespace/]name objects
                                          (repeatable; combine with --select-setting)
      --select-setting strings            import only these top-level settings sections
                                          (repeatable; combine with --select-object)
      --skip-settings                     leave settings unchanged
      --source-insecure-skip-tls-verify   skip source TLS verification for a lab with a
                                          self-signed certificate
      --source-key-file string            file containing the source v6 application password
                                          (otherwise $PIHOLE_APP_PASSWORD)
      --source-url string                 source console URL (including any reverse-proxy prefix)
      --update-nameservers                use the destination context hostname or IP for
                                          imported authority
      --use-vips                          use discovered kudurru VIPs for nameservers and
                                          address records
      --wait                              wait for the background import and report its final
                                          results (requires --apply)
```

### kudurru import runs

List migration runs or inspect a run and its cutovers.

```text
kudurru import runs [id]
```

## kudurru lameduck

Put the local kudurru into lameduck through the ops listener (POST /lameduck, loopback only) and wait for the duration, if one is given, so the edge's health checks (dnsdist must-resolve on health.kudurru.internal., every second) and the Kubernetes endpoints take the node out before it stops. Queries that still arrive are answered. --cancel leaves lameduck.

In Kubernetes use it as the preStop hook: lifecycle: { preStop: { exec: { command: \["kudurru", "lameduck", "5s"\] } } }

```text
kudurru lameduck [duration] [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru lameduck 5s
kudurru lameduck --cancel
```

Flags:

```text
      --cancel               leave lameduck
      --ops-address string   ops listener of the local node (loopback) (default "127.0.0.1:8081")
      --timeout duration     request timeout (default 3s)
```

## kudurru license

kudurru is source-available under the Kudurru Community License (LICENSE). Running it for eligible personal or nonprofit use is free; business and government production needs an agreement. Enterprise materials have their own notice; commercial features depend on the Order Form. A key unlocks more than one node, more than one policy and the features under ee/ (OIDC single sign-on, the dnsdist and keepalived edge, the integrations). A free personal key covers 3 nodes. See https://kudurru.io/license.

The key is read from --license-key, KUDURRU\_LICENSE\_KEY, the file KUDURRU\_LICENSE\_KEY\_FILE names, or &lt;node.dataDir&gt;/license.key, in that order. Licensing never affects DNS answering: without a key the node serves DNS as usual and only the node limit, the policy limit and the licensed features apply.

### kudurru license status

Show the license this node would run with.

```text
kudurru license status [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --json                 print as JSON
      --license-key string   check this key instead of the configured sources
```

### kudurru license verify

Verify a key and print what it grants (- reads the key from stdin).

```text
kudurru license verify KEY|-
```

## kudurru login

Log in to a kudurru API server and save the endpoint as a named context in ~/.config/kudurru/config.yaml.

With --token the API token is verified (GET /auth/me) and stored. With --username the local password is exchanged for a session (POST /auth/login), which then mints an API token for the CLI (POST /auth/tokens). Tokens go to the OS keyring; when no keyring is available (headless Linux, containers) they are kept in the config file, which is written with mode 0600. Set KUDURRU\_KEYRING=file to skip the keyring.

For an enrolled authenticator, add --totp for a hidden terminal prompt, or --password-stdin --totp-stdin to read password and code as two lines. Codes must contain six ASCII digits. Login is attempted once, without redirects or automatic retries.

```text
kudurru login --server https://dns.example [--token kdr_… | --username admin] [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru login --server https://dns.example --token kdr_abc123def456_…
kudurru login --server https://dns.example --username admin
kudurru login --server https://dns.example --token-stdin < token.txt
echo "$PW" | kudurru login --server http://127.0.0.1:8080 --username admin --password-stdin --name local
```

Flags:

```text
      --default-namespace string   default namespace stored in the context
      --name string                context name (default: the server host)
  -p, --password string            password (prefer the prompt or --password-stdin)
      --password-stdin             read the password from stdin
      --token-expires-in string    lifetime of the minted token, e.g. 720h (default: the server's)
      --token-name string          name of the token minted for the CLI (default
                                   kudurru-cli@<hostname>)
      --token-stdin                read the API token from stdin (keeps it out of the process list)
      --totp                       prompt for a six-digit authenticator code without echo
      --totp-stdin                 read the authenticator code from stdin (after the password
                                   with --password-stdin)
  -u, --username string            local account to log in with
```

## kudurru logout

Forget the stored token of a context.

```text
kudurru logout [context] [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --remove   also delete the context
```

## kudurru logs

Show the query log; --follow streams new queries.

```text
kudurru logs [flags]
```

Aliases: `log`, `querylog`.

Examples:

```sh
kudurru logs --client 192.168.1.23 --limit 100
kudurru logs --domain '*.doubleclick.net' --status-class blocked
kudurru logs -f --status blocked_list
```

Flags:

```text
      --client string         client IP, CIDR or name (* wildcards)
      --domain string         domain, exact or with * wildcards
  -f, --follow                stream new queries (SSE) after the last page
      --limit int             number of past queries to show (0 with --follow: only new ones)
                              (default 50)
      --list string           list name
      --no-headers            omit the header line
      --qtype string          query type, e.g. AAAA
      --since string          start: RFC 3339 or a duration back from now (1h)
      --status strings        statuses to keep (comma-separated), e.g. blocked_list,cached
      --status-class string   status class: permitted, blocked, cached, error, ...
      --until string          end: RFC 3339 or a duration back from now
      --upstream string       upstream name
      --zone string           zone name
```

## kudurru query

Resolve a name through the server's own pipeline (POST /api/v1/dns/query) and print the answer the way dig does, plus kudurru's verdict: status, upstream, and the list and rule when a query was blocked. --client evaluates the policy of another client address.

```text
kudurru query <name> [type] [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru query example.com
kudurru query ads.example.net AAAA --client 192.168.1.23
```

Flags:

```text
      --client string   evaluate policy as this client IP
```

## kudurru records

List, add and remove records in a zone.

Aliases: `record`, `rr`.

### kudurru records add

Create or replace one endpoint (name, type and its targets) in a record set of the zone. The record set defaults to "api-&lt;zone&gt;" and is created on demand. Targets are in presentation format: an address for A/AAAA, a name for CNAME, "10 mail.example.com." for MX, a quoted string for TXT.

```text
kudurru records add <zone> <name> <type> <target...> [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru records add home-example-com nas.home.example.com A 192.168.1.10 --ttl 300
kudurru records add home-example-com home.example.com MX "10 mail.home.example.com."
```

Flags:

```text
      --comment string          comment stored with the record
      --record-set string       record set to write (default api-<zone>)
      --set-identifier string   external-dns set identifier
      --ttl int                 record TTL in seconds (default: the zone's defaultTTL)
```

### kudurru records list

List a zone's records across its record sets.

```text
kudurru records list <zone>
```

Aliases: `ls`.

### kudurru records rm

Remove one name/type from a zone.

```text
kudurru records rm <zone> <name> <type> [flags]
```

Aliases: `remove`, `delete`.

Flags:

```text
      --record-set string       only this record set (namespace/name or name)
      --set-identifier string   only the endpoint with this set identifier
```

Re-apply a backup (POST /apply; per-object results).

```text
kudurru restore -f file.yaml [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
  -f, --filename stringArray   backup file, or - for stdin
```

## kudurru serve

Run the kudurru node: the store (sqlite or kube), first-boot bootstrap, file-managed objects, zonecache, the query pipeline (ingress, authoritative, cache, upstream) on every configured transport, the Lease-elected controller, the ops and metrics listeners. The API and UI land in milestone M3.

```text
kudurru serve [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --license-key string   license key (or KUDURRU_LICENSE_KEY, KUDURRU_LICENSE_KEY_FILE,
                             <node.dataDir>/license.key); without one kudurru runs with the
                             community license
```

## kudurru settings

Read and change runtime settings (cluster keys and this node's keys).

### kudurru settings adopt

adopt upstream settings ownership. Read the revision with `kudurru settings ownership`. Before release, export with `kudurru settings yaml upstreams`, commit and apply those Helm values, then read the updated revision. Release refuses a handoff if the file settings differ.

```text
kudurru settings adopt upstreams [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --revision string   reviewed revision from settings ownership
```

### kudurru settings get

Show settings (redacted) with their scope.

```text
kudurru settings get [key...] [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --scope string   only cluster or node keys
```

### kudurru settings ownership

Show section ownership and revisions.

```text
kudurru settings ownership
```

### kudurru settings release

release upstream settings ownership. Read the revision with `kudurru settings ownership`. Before release, export with `kudurru settings yaml upstreams`, commit and apply those Helm values, then read the updated revision. Release refuses a handoff if the file settings differ.

```text
kudurru settings release upstreams [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --revision string   reviewed revision from settings ownership
```

### kudurru settings set

Change settings with a JSON merge patch. Cluster-scope keys go to PATCH /api/v1/settings and apply to every node; node-scope keys go to PATCH /api/v1/node/config on the node that serves the request. hostOnly keys (listener addresses, dataDir, ...) can never be set through the API: put them in kudurru.yaml or the KUDURRU\_&lt;SECTION&gt;\_\_&lt;KEY&gt; environment variable on the host. "key-" removes the override so the default applies again.

For safe concurrent upstream edits, run kudurru settings ownership to review the revision and pass it with --revision. Omitting --revision preserves legacy behavior: your upstream edit can overwrite values changed since you reviewed them.

```text
kudurru settings set key=value... [key-] [flags]
```

Examples:

```sh
kudurru settings set cache.maxEntries=200000
kudurru settings set blocking.refreshInterval=12h log.level=debug
kudurru settings set upstreams.bootstrap=9.9.9.9,1.1.1.1
kudurru settings set log.level-
```

Flags:

```text
      --revision string   reviewed upstreams revision from settings ownership (If-Match)
```

### kudurru settings yaml

Generate Helm values without saving (optionally from a proposed JSON section).

```text
kudurru settings yaml upstreams [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --proposed-file string   complete proposed upstreams section as JSON
```

## kudurru vip

keepalived supervisor and VIP tools (PID 1 of the kudurru-keepalived image).

### kudurru vip drain

Move VIPs off this node for maintenance (track file 300); --undo writes 0.

```text
kudurru vip drain <vip>... [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --run-dir string   shared run directory (default "/run/kudurru")
      --undo             end the drain (weight 0)
```

### kudurru vip fifo

Consume keepalived's notify FIFO (run by keepalived as vrrp\_notify\_fifo\_script).

```text
kudurru vip fifo [--node name] [--run-dir dir] <fifo> [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --node string      node name (keepalived router_id)
      --run-dir string   directory of vip-state.json (default "/run/kudurru")
```

### kudurru vip probe

Queries --qname over udp and tcp on the VIP while this node holds it (loopback otherwise) and requires --require-backends backends up in the local dnsdist. keepalived runs it every second with a 1 s timeout.

```text
kudurru vip probe [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --dns string                              VIP address:port to probe over udp and tcp
                                                (loopback is probed while this node does not
                                                hold the VIP)
      --dnsdist-api string                      local dnsdist API; empty skips the backend
                                                check (default "http://127.0.0.1:8083")
      --dnsdist-api-key-file kudurru edge run   dnsdist API key published by kudurru edge run
                                                (default "/run/kudurru/dnsdist-api.key")
      --qname string                            name queried for TXT (default
                                                "health.kudurru.internal.")
      --require-backends int                    minimum number of dnsdist backends up (default 1)
      --timeout duration                        overall probe timeout (keepalived's script
                                                timeout is 1 s) (default 900ms)
```

### kudurru vip rebalance

Hand VIPs this node holds but does not prefer back to their preferred node (writes 300, then 0).

```text
kudurru vip rebalance [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --run-dir string     shared run directory (default "/run/kudurru")
      --timeout duration   how long to wait for keepalived to leave MASTER (default 30s)
      --vip strings        move these VIPs (if held) regardless of priority
```

### kudurru vip render

Print the keepalived.conf the supervisor would run.

```text
kudurru vip render [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --dnsdist-api-key-file kudurru edge run   dnsdist API key file written by kudurru edge
                                                run (default "/run/kudurru/dnsdist-api.key")
      --hmac-key-file string                    auth_hmac key file; {vrid} is replaced by the
                                                VRID (default "/run/secrets/vrrp_hmac_{vrid}")
      --kudurru-bin string                      kudurru path used in rendered scripts
                                                (root-owned for enable_script_security)
                                                (default "/usr/local/bin/kudurru")
      --legacy                                  keepalived 2.3.x: render without auth_hmac
                                                (adverts unauthenticated)
      --node-count int                          number of nodes (default: peers + 1)
      --node-name string                        alias of --router-id (the chart passes
                                                spec.nodeName)
      --peers strings                           the other nodes' unicast addresses
      --peers-file string                       file with one peer address per line, watched:
                                                re-render + SIGHUP on change (overrides --peers)
      --peers-from string                       nodes:<label selector>: peers are the selected
                                                Kubernetes Nodes' InternalIPs (this node
                                                excluded), re-listed every 30 s; the priority
                                                index defaults to this node's position by name
                                                (or its kudurru.io/vip-priority-index label)
      --preempt-delay stringArray               name=seconds: preempt_delay instead of
                                                nopreempt for that VIP
      --priority-index int                      this node's index: priority 200-10*index for
                                                the first VIP
      --probe-command string                    VRRP check command prefix rendered into
                                                vrrp_script (e.g. "/usr/local/bin/kudurru
                                                health --vrrp") (default
                                                "/usr/local/bin/kudurru health --vrrp")
      --require-backends int                    backends that must be up for this node to hold
                                                a VIP (default 1)
      --router-id string                        node name (router_id); default
                                                $KUDURRU_NODE__NAME or the host name
      --run-dir string                          shared run directory: FIFO, track files,
                                                state, dnsdist API key (default "/run/kudurru")
      --track-dnsdist-api string                dnsdist API the VRRP probe checks (default
                                                "http://127.0.0.1:8083")
      --unicast-src string                      this node's VRRP source address (default: the
                                                first address of --vrrp-interface, or the
                                                first VIP's interface)
      --vip stringArray                         VIP as name=addr/len@iface#vrid (repeatable;
                                                the second VIP gets reversed priorities); the
                                                VRID is host-only and never changes
      --vrrp-interface string                   interface for VRRP advertisements (default:
                                                each VIP's interface); VIP addresses stay on
                                                the interfaces in --vip
```

### kudurru vip run

Render, keepalived -t, exec and supervise keepalived; SIGHUP on re-render.

```text
kudurru vip run [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --config-path string                      rendered configuration (default
                                                "/etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf")
      --dnsdist-api-key-file kudurru edge run   dnsdist API key file written by kudurru edge
                                                run (default "/run/kudurru/dnsdist-api.key")
      --health-address string                   supervisor listener: /healthz/ready,
                                                /healthz/live, /status, /metrics (default ":8085")
      --hmac-key-file string                    auth_hmac key file; {vrid} is replaced by the
                                                VRID (default "/run/secrets/vrrp_hmac_{vrid}")
      --keepalived-bin string                   keepalived executable (default "keepalived")
      --kudurru-bin string                      kudurru path used in rendered scripts
                                                (root-owned for enable_script_security)
                                                (default "/usr/local/bin/kudurru")
      --legacy                                  keepalived 2.3.x: render without auth_hmac
                                                (adverts unauthenticated)
      --log-format string                       json or text (default "json")
      --log-level string                        debug, info, warn or error (default "info")
      --node-count int                          number of nodes (default: peers + 1)
      --node-name string                        alias of --router-id (the chart passes
                                                spec.nodeName)
      --peers strings                           the other nodes' unicast addresses
      --peers-file string                       file with one peer address per line, watched:
                                                re-render + SIGHUP on change (overrides --peers)
      --peers-from string                       nodes:<label selector>: peers are the selected
                                                Kubernetes Nodes' InternalIPs (this node
                                                excluded), re-listed every 30 s; the priority
                                                index defaults to this node's position by name
                                                (or its kudurru.io/vip-priority-index label)
      --preempt-delay stringArray               name=seconds: preempt_delay instead of
                                                nopreempt for that VIP
      --priority-index int                      this node's index: priority 200-10*index for
                                                the first VIP
      --probe-command string                    VRRP check command prefix rendered into
                                                vrrp_script (e.g. "/usr/local/bin/kudurru
                                                health --vrrp") (default
                                                "/usr/local/bin/kudurru health --vrrp")
      --require-backends int                    backends that must be up for this node to hold
                                                a VIP (default 1)
      --router-id string                        node name (router_id); default
                                                $KUDURRU_NODE__NAME or the host name
      --run-dir string                          shared run directory: FIFO, track files,
                                                state, dnsdist API key (default "/run/kudurru")
      --stop-timeout duration                   keepalived SIGTERM grace period (keep below
                                                the container stop grace period) (default 15s)
      --track-dnsdist-api string                dnsdist API the VRRP probe checks (default
                                                "http://127.0.0.1:8083")
      --unicast-src string                      this node's VRRP source address (default: the
                                                first address of --vrrp-interface, or the
                                                first VIP's interface)
      --vip stringArray                         VIP as name=addr/len@iface#vrid (repeatable;
                                                the second VIP gets reversed priorities); the
                                                VRID is host-only and never changes
      --vrrp-interface string                   interface for VRRP advertisements (default:
                                                each VIP's interface); VIP addresses stay on
                                                the interfaces in --vip
```

## kudurru zones

List, import, export, notify and delete zones.

Aliases: `zone`.

### kudurru zones delete

Delete a zone and every record set that references it.

```text
kudurru zones delete <zone> [flags]
```

Aliases: `rm`.

Flags:

```text
      --dry-run   only report what would be deleted
```

### kudurru zones export

Print a zone in BIND presentation format.

```text
kudurru zones export <zone> [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
      --out string   write to this file instead of stdout
```

### kudurru zones get

Show one zone.

```text
kudurru zones get <zone>
```

### kudurru zones import

Import a BIND zone file into a zone's record sets.

```text
kudurru zones import <zone> -f file.zone [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
  -f, --filename string   zone file in BIND presentation format, or - for stdin
      --origin string     zone apex, to create the DNSZone when it does not exist yet
```

### kudurru zones list

List zones with serial, record count and readiness.

```text
kudurru zones list
```

Aliases: `ls`.

### kudurru zones notify

Send NOTIFY for a zone to its secondaries.

```text
kudurru zones notify <zone>
```

### kudurru zones options

Review and replace zone options with a resource-version check.

#### kudurru zones options get

Show the zone specification and its reviewed resource version.

```text
kudurru zones options get <zone>
```

#### kudurru zones options set

Replace the complete spec using the resourceVersion emitted by zones options get. Metadata and status are preserved. A concurrent change, missing permission or another manager's ownership is refused; this command never retries the write. Use zones options get -o yaml, edit spec, then pass that document with -f.

```text
kudurru zones options set <zone> -f options.yaml [flags]
```

Flags:

```text
  -f, --file string   reviewed YAML/JSON options document, or - for stdin
```
